reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes Forsage participation as a route to income, encouraging invitations to friends and describing income from putting specified amounts into the program. The speaker links those amounts to immediate full distribution and describes a bottom-to-top income mechanism using ponzi or pyramid terminology. The meeting’s calls for honesty do not resolve the basis of these income and distribution claims; the separate sponsored miner ad has no established connection to the meeting.

citations.quote: matrix of X4
the maximum he will get income in both slots
You will get overspill

opening.argument: Judge, consider the speaker’s instructions alongside the income claims. Participants are told not to give fake information, to understand people’s actual needs, and to explain the differences honestly. Those are meaningful qualifications in a meeting about an income opportunity. The speaker does not present deception as an acceptable way to bring people in. The promotional tone warrants scrutiny, but it should not erase the explicit direction to communicate accurately.

citations.quote: No need to give fake information or motivation to anyone. Understand their actual need.
I have to do everything with honesty
whatever you have done, explain to people very well, tell the difference

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s matrix and slot-income quotations show what the speakers discuss; they do not, on their own, show a guaranteed return or an instruction to mislead recruits. The invitation to friends is also accompanied by a direction to understand their actual needs. That omitted context matters when judging whether the presentation is deceptive rather than merely favorable to Forsage.

citations.quote: the maximum he will get income in both slots
you invite your friends and plan for them, maybe they too are facing these problems.
No need to give fake information or motivation to anyone. Understand their actual need.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An instruction not to lie does not change what is being promoted. The speaker encourages invitations to friends, describes income from matrix slots, and tells participants they will receive overspill. Honest-sounding conduct advice does not establish that those recruitment-linked income claims are reliable or that the presentation is merely a warning.

the maximum he will get income in both slots

opening.argument: Judge, this is also a comparative technical presentation. A speaker says a purportedly decentralized project must be checked, walks through a contract address, and raises the absence of a published audit report. The presentation discusses how a matrix works rather than simply displaying an earnings claim. The sampled contract-explorer screen supports the reading that viewers are being shown information to examine. Although the meeting favors Forsage, its technical comparison and stated concerns give the material a substantial explanatory purpose; describing possible income within that explanation should not automatically be treated as a direct solicitation.

citations.quote: There it is the decentralized project. First we will have to check it.
the contract address of the post has been placed, then this is about the contract now we will get a lot of information
there are no talks about the audit report so far

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution isolates slot income from the surrounding explanation. The speaker also calls for checking a project and discusses an unpublished audit report. Those details do not prove Forsage is sound, but they do show that the meeting includes comparison and examination, not just an unqualified instruction to invest. The separate ad on the displayed page adds nothing to whether the meeting itself solicits viewers.

citations.quote: First we will have to check it.
there are no talks about the audit report so far

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical explanation does not make the presentation neutral. The meeting tells participants to invite friends and implement what they are taught, while explaining income from slots and overspill. Examining another project’s contract or audit does not neutralize the favorable recruitment-and-income pitch for Forsage.

opening.argument: Judge, the title promises details about other platforms, and the description calls Forsage a business while saying no sale or purchase is needed. The spoken comparison likewise says there is no need to buy or sell anything. The speakers mention amounts and possible income, so those claims deserve scrutiny; nevertheless, the supplied material does not show a viewer being given payment instructions, asked for credentials, or promised a guaranteed personal return. Without treating a favorable business presentation as proof of every missing step, the record supports discussion of a business opportunity rather than a demonstrated attempt to take a viewer’s money.

citations.quote: FULL DETAILS OF OTHER PLATFORMS IN HINDI!
Doing BUSINESS in FORSAGE is very easy
No need to SELL anything, no PURCHASING
There is no need to buy or sell anything.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution fairly points to amounts, slots, and overspill, but those passages do not supply an instruction for this viewer to transfer funds or a guaranteed return for joining. The description’s denial of a required sale or purchase cannot prove the opportunity safe; equally, the income terminology alone should not substitute for showing how this video obtains money through deception.

citations.quote: you put 100 rupees in forces, you put 1000, you put 50000
the maximum he will get income in both slots
No need to SELL anything, no PURCHASING

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A product sale is not the mechanism at issue. The speaker describes putting money into Forsage, receiving income through slots, and getting overspill. The absence of a credential request or step-by-step payment instruction does not undo the video’s promotion of participation-linked financial rewards.
